How the Moldova Red Cross became part of everyday life for Ukrainian refugees
Language classes, a psychologist, a knitting club: four families from Ukraine on what the Moldova Red Cross means to them today.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network.
Our secretariat supports local Red Cross and Red Crescent action in more than 191 countries, bringing together more than 18 million volunteers for the good of humanity.

Latest emergencies
Yemen: Population Movement 2026
Escalating conflict in Yemen has forced thousands of families to flee their homes and left many people injured, with urgent needs for medical care, food, shelter, clean water and protection. Yemen Red Crescent Society (YRCS) volunteers and teams are running ambulances around the clock, providing first aid and delivering relief to displaced families. The IFRC has launched an Emergency Appeal on behalf of the YRCS to scale up this lifesaving support. Donate now: your gift goes to the IFRC, which channels it to the YRCS and remains accountable for how it is used, so help reaches the people who need it most.

Nepal: Flash Floods 2026
Flash floods tore through northern Nepal on 26 August, claiming hundreds of lives, destroying homes, roads and bridges, and leaving entire communities displaces and cut off. The Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) is on the ground delivering clean water, shelter, first aid and emergency supplies.Donate today to help IFRC and the NRCS to scale up their response and bring life-saving assistance to those who need it most. Donations are made to the IFRC, which will channel resources to the NRCS and ensure accountability for their use.Read more: IFRC launches CHF 25 million Emergency Appeal in response to devastating Nepal flash floods

Colombia: Earthquake 2026
A magnitude 7.4 earthquake has devastated western Colombia, killing at least 176 people, injuring thousands more, and leaving families without homes, clean water, or medical care across 14 departments. Colombian Red Cross teams are on the ground right now — carrying out search and rescue, treating the injured, reuniting separated families, and getting emergency shelter and aid to those whohave lost everything — but the scale of destruction is outpacing what they can do alone.IFRC has launched an emergency appeal to support the response activities of the Colombian Red Cross. Donations are made to the IFRC, which will channel resources to its member National Society and ensure accountability for their use.Donate today to help IFRC and the Colombian Red Cross scale up their response and bring life-saving assistance to those who need it most.

Venezuela: Earthquake 2026
Two powerful earthquakes have struck Venezuela, severely affecting Gran Caracas and La Guaira, and causing widespread destruction across the capital and surrounding areas. The Venezuelan Red Cross is on the ground, carrying out search and rescue operations, assisting the injured, and assessing urgent and growing needs.IFRC has launched an emergency appeal to support the response activities of the Venezuelan Red Cross. Donations are made to the IFRC, which will channel resources to its member National Society and ensure accountability for their use.Donate today to help IFRC and VRC scale up their response and bring life-saving assistance to those who need it most.

Africa: Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak 2026
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is rapidly escalating, with cases and deaths continuing to rise as the virus spreads across multiple provinces and into neighboring Uganda. Families and communities urgently need access to reliable health information, early detection, safe burials, and lifesaving public health support to prevent further transmission and protect overwhelmed health systems. Donate today to help the DRC and Uganda Red Cross Societies to provide life-saving assistance.Read more: IFRC delivers critical supplies to eastern DRC amid ongoing Ebola outbreak

Our Global Plan for 2026
IFRC Global Plan 2026
The IFRC’s Global Plan 2026addresses the world’s most pressing humanitarian issues and outlines how the IFRC – as a global network of local actors – is evolving to place more resources and expertise closer to its 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. The IFRC’s support for local humanitarian action is needed more than ever in a rapidly changing world where increasing numbers of people are placed at risk by climate extremes, disasters, health crises, displacement and other threats to their safety, security and wellbeing. The Global Planoutlines how the IFRC is evolving to ensure National Societies and their 17 million community-based volunteers are able to meet and address these challenges. In 2026, wherever people are at risk, the IFRC will work to empower the locally led humanitarian action that supports communities in crisis and builds the lasting resilience that reduces future needs.The executive summary of the plan is available here.
